test.summary: 2(b) fail-restart with Permian cold: test RMSE 6,282 MW vs plant cold 1,164; weather-free margins 0.20 (tent) / 2.14 (hours). Drivers correlate r = 0.78 (Feb 10–19), so the comparison rests on timing. Not supported by this model, not refuted: the Permian went below freezing first (02-10 07:00 vs 02-12 00:00 at the plants), and storage and pipeline pressure buffer supply for a while; a model with no delay term can't use that lead. | Adding Texas production loss (FERC Fig. 35, a Tier 2 chart read) as a second failure driver does not improve the out-of-sample fit: test RMSE 1,725 MW vs 1,164 cold only (needs ≤ 932). Fitted γ = 0.0101. About 13 storm days: a direction, not an estimate.

tests.summary: 2(b) fail-restart with Permian cold: test RMSE 6,282 MW vs plant cold 1,164; weather-free margins 0.20 (tent) / 2.14 (hours). Drivers correlate r = 0.78 (Feb 10–19), so the comparison rests on timing. Not supported by this model, not refuted: the Permian went below freezing first (02-10 07:00 vs 02-12 00:00 at the plants), and storage and pipeline pressure buffer supply for a while; a model with no delay term can't use that lead.

Adding Texas production loss (FERC Fig. 35, a Tier 2 chart read) as a second failure driver does not improve the out-of-sample fit: test RMSE 1,725 MW vs 1,164 cold only (needs ≤ 932). Fitted γ = 0.0101. About 13 storm days: a direction, not an estimate.

test.summary: Untestable with Tier 0: nothing measures power delivered to gas facilities, and FERC says the extent is unknown. Text evidence: FERC attributes 18.1% of the gas production decline on Feb 14 (before any firm load shed) and 21.6% on Feb 17 (the day of maximum losses) to loss of power, 23.5% over the whole event; Enverus's survey names loss of power as the most cited cause. The earlier event study (shed jump at 2/15 01:59 vs gas outages) was inconclusive because gas outages were already climbing before the shock (the design check's pretrend).
